title: Arkret Direct Conversation Operations
description: Closed carriers for the Direct Conversation resolver and single-sided founding. Creation is never carried here: a Direct Conversation Realm is created only by the founder derived from the pair's root Contact round through the direct_conversation_genesis admission variant of ak.realm.create.

direct_conversation_coordinates.description: Permanent Direct Conversation coordinates. binding_event_ref appears only from found or suspended onward; it is absent while the pair is still provisional.

direct_conversation_founding_acceptance_.description: Source-signed evidence that the founder current Principal Server atomically accepted exactly one Direct Conversation founding unit and closed its local unique slot. It creates no Realm, authorizes no Message and is not a global slot; a second receipt for the same pair and founder but a different unit is direct_conversation_pair_materialization_conflict evidence. proof signs the closed transcript H("ak.direct-conversation.founding-receipt.v1", this object without proof); the receiver recomputes that preimage from the receipt fields and never trusts a carried digest. proof.verification_method resolves to the issuer_service_id current service key at accepted_at and proof.created_at equals accepted_at.

direct_conversation_founding_input.description: Verbatim authoring material for the founding unit the caller is now entitled to author, carried only by the creation_required outcome. Member names equal the DirectConversationFoundingUnitSubmission members byte for byte, so the caller copies them across without any renaming map (service-http-binding.md 2.2.2 echo-container discipline). The caller still authors and signs all four Events itself; this container never carries Event bytes, coordinates or a receipt. Material that the service cannot assemble or verify yields temporarily_unavailable instead of a creation_required outcome without it.

founding_authority_evidence.description: The human branch for a peer Contact founding and the controller_agent branch for an own-Agent founding; the service selects the branch that matches this pair and never returns both.

direct_conversation_resolve_outcome.description: Closed tagged outcome of ak.self.direct_conversation.read.resolve. Evaluation order is fixed: temporarily_unavailable when the current basis or founder cannot be verified; then creation_blocked, creation_required or awaiting_founder while no Realm exists; then suspended for identity, materialization, terminal or gate conflicts; then provisional while no binding endorsement exists; found last. awaiting_founder never transfers authority by timeout, recovery policy, successor designation or permanent-unavailability inference; v1 defines no founder_unrecoverable state.

active_mls_generation_value_digest.description: SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS for the complete currently accepted ak.component.direct_conversation.active_mls_generation.v1 cell value. The Event ref and whole-value digest are supplied or omitted as one pair.
SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS for the complete currently accepted active-generation cell value, not a hash of active_mls_generation_ref.
Present with active_mls_generation_ref whenever an accepted active-generation cell exists, including the replacement-repair suspended state.

direct_conversation_resolve_request.description: Closed query body for ak.self.direct_conversation.read.resolve. Creation is never carried here: a Direct Conversation Realm is created only by the derived founder through the direct_conversation_genesis admission variant of ak.realm.create.

direct_conversation_repair_authorization.description: Requester-owned detached authorization over UTF8('ak.direct-conversation-repair-dispatch-v1\n') || RFC8785_JCS({request_id,content}). The branch identity, verification method and authorization Event MUST match the content and the portable evidence byte for byte. The source service session and the outer source-service signature are transport gates, never substitutes for this participant signature.

direct_conversation_repair_requester_evi.description: Closed requester-kind discriminator. Human-device and Native-Agent authority is verified from the accepted rejoin/KeyPackage Events and their in-envelope Principal Server admission proofs; no signer-evidence sidecar is accepted.

direct_conversation_repair_dispatch_requ.description: Authenticated self command. The requester submits one stable request identity, exact non-authorizing repair content and its own detached authorization. It never enumerates recipient devices; the source service validates current gates and relays the exact request to the peer's current accepted Principal Server.

direct_conversation_repair_relay_request.description: Service-to-service repair relay. The source service copies request_id, content and requester_authorization byte for byte from the accepted self dispatch, appends exactly one portable current-authority evidence branch, then covers the canonical body with RFC 9421 and Content-Digest. The destination independently verifies participant authority and every durable Event gate.

direct_conversation_repair_enqueue_outco.description: Byte-identical terminal outcome proving only that the destination service durably accepted this exact relay and atomically completed exactly one closed recipient target branch. A human principal freezes and enqueues every current authorized device; a Native Agent freezes and enqueues its one current active runtime endpoint from accepted agent-key/session binding and never invents an ak:device identity. The branch-specific digest commits the frozen fanout without disclosing target ids. It is not a repair acknowledgement and says nothing about later Commit, Welcome or activation.

request_digest.description: SHA-256 of the exact canonical direct_conversation_repair_relay_request body.

target_snapshot_digest.description: H('ak.member-repair-target-snapshot-native-agent-v1', {recipient_agent_id,active_runtime_endpoint_ref,device_message_id}), where the endpoint is the one current accepted agent-key/session binding endpoint.

direct_conversation_send_blocker.description: Closed machine-readable blocker set surfaced by the Direct Conversation resolver. Every value MUST be server-verifiable: the service MUST be able to prove it from accepted authoritative state it may lawfully read, and it MUST NOT guess, decrypt or relay a client self-report. personal_blocked and history_key_unavailable are deliberately absent and MUST NOT be re-added: ak.account.blocklist is holder-private account data that a synchronizing service only ever sees encrypted to holder devices, and whether a historical MLS secret is installed is device-private key state, so a service that answered either one would have to break the encryption invariant or accept an unauthenticated claim as authority. They live in the client-local blocker set of ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 instead, and a reply carrying either value is a schema_violation the client MUST reject rather than tolerate. presence_offline and keypackage_empty stay here because the service does hold provable facts for them, but they MUST be returned only to an existing exact-pair participant of that very pair; every other caller MUST receive the same opaque failure as for a pair that does not exist, so neither value can be used to enumerate or probe a non-participant. Values never disclose peer presence to non-participants.
